It was said: the governing element in such a construction is an elided verb indicated by the meaning, i.e., "look at him in the state of his shaykh-hood," so the demonstrative is not the governor nor the particle of alerting, if there is one there. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "We recite them" contains an elided noun, i.e., we recite its matter and explain the lesson in it. It may be that by "verses of Allah" is meant the Qur'an revealed with these meanings, so there is no elided noun in "we recite them." End. "We recite them" means: the King orders that we recite them. It was read "yatluwha" with the third person, referring to Allah. "Bil-haqq": with truth, because its soundness is known by rational proofs.

﴿Then in what statement﴾ the verse: it contains rebuke, reproach and threat. (After Allah): i.e., after the statement of Allah, which is His Book and His speech, like His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book similar in its parts﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and He said: (p-44) ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], i.e., after the statement of Allah and His speech. Al-Dahhak said: after the monotheism of Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: "after Allah and His verses," i.e., after the verses of Allah, like their saying: "Zayd pleased me and his generosity," meaning: "the generosity of Zayd pleased me." End. This is nothing, because in terms of meaning it involves inserting nouns without necessity, and conjunction, while the intended meaning is other than conjunction, bringing it into the category of apposition, since the estimate "the generosity of Zayd" applies only to "Zayd pleased me, his generosity," without "wa," as apposition; and this is a reversal of the realities of grammar. Rather, the meaning of "Zayd pleased me and his generosity" is that Zayd's person pleased him and his generosity pleased him, so they are two pleasures, not one pleasure; and we have already responded to his like of this saying previously. Abu Ja'far, al-A'raj, Shaybah, Qatadah, the two Harami, Abu 'Amr, and 'Asim in one transmission read "yu'minun" with the third person by yaa'; al-A'mash and the rest of the seven read it with the second person by ta' of address; Talhah read "tuqinun" with ta' on top and qaf from iqan.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, and it was said: concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and what he used to buy of the stories of non-Arabs and occupy people with them instead of listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general concerning whoever harms the religion of Allah. "Affak" and "athim" are intensive adjectives; the discussion of the words of this verse has preceded. Al-Jumhur read "'alima," and Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq read it with a damma on the 'ayn and shadda on the lam, passive, meaning: "he came to know." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the meaning of "thumma" in His saying ﴿then persists﴾? I say: its meaning is like its meaning in the saying of the speaker:
"He sees the surges of death, then visits them,"
because the surges of death are of the sort that the one who sees them should escape by himself and seek flight from them; as for visiting them and advancing to engage with them, this is something far-fetched. So the meaning of "thumma" is the indication that the act of advancing upon them after seeing them and witnessing them is something that is deemed unlikely by custom and nature. Likewise the clear and decisive signs of Allah which are established by truth: whoever has them recited to him and hears them, his persistence in error in their presence and his arrogance against believing in them is deemed unlikely by the intellects.

(p-٤٥)

﴿He took them in mockery﴾. He did not say "took it," indicating that when he perceives any part of the speech to be among the verses that Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), he plunges into mocking all the verses, and does not restrict his mockery to what has reached him. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And when he learns something of Our verses﴾ means that the obstinate person can seize upon it and make it a pretext by which he climbs to slander and defamation. He fabricates it and takes the verses of Allah in mockery. This is like Ibn al-Zib'ara's fabrication of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], and his sophistry toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "I have defeated you." The pronoun may also refer to a thing, because it carries the meaning of the verse, like the saying of Abu al-Atahiya:

"My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the Guided Upright One suffice for it,"

where he meant ʿUtba. End of quotation. ʿUtba was a slave girl whom Abu al-Atahiya loved and to whom he was attached.

The demonstrative ﴿those﴾ refers to every liar, because it encompasses the liars. It is first treated according to the wording of "kull" (every), then it is put in the singular according to meaning and then in the plural, like His saying: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoices﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53].

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾: that is, before them. "Waraʾ" means what is hidden from behind and in front.

﴿Nor will what they earned avail them anything﴾ of wealth in their trade, ﴿nor what they took as protectors besides Allah﴾ of idols. ﴿This﴾, that is the Qur'an, ﴿is guidance﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in guidance, like your saying: "This is a man," meaning he is complete in manhood. Talha, Ibn Muhaysin, the people of Makkah, Ibn Kathir and Hafs read ﴿painful﴾ in the nominative as an adjective of ʿadhab (punishment). Al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, ʿIsa, al-Aʿmash and the rest of the seven read it in the genitive as an adjective of rijz (torment).

﴿Allah is He who subjected﴾, the verse: it is a verse of reflection on the subjection of this great creation and the ships that run in it, by this lowly creation, which is the human being. ﴿By His command﴾: that is, by His power. He put the command in the place of power, as if He commands the ships to run. ﴿From His bounty﴾ through trade, diving for pearls and coral, and extracting fresh flesh. ﴿What is in the heavens﴾ of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, winds and air, and the angels entrusted with all of this. ﴿And what is in the earth﴾ of animals, waters, mountains and plants.

The majority read ﴿from Him﴾ (minhu). Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a kasra on the mim, a shadda on the nun, and a fatha on the ta' (tā'), as a verbal noun (maṣdar). Abu Hatim said: attributing this reading to Ibn ʿAbbas is an injustice. Abu al-Fath related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, al-Jahdari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and Sahib al-Lawamih also related it from these four. Ibn Khalawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Salama ibn Muharib read likewise, except that he put a damma on the ta', meaning "He is from Him." He also read with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the nun. The pronoun of attribution refers to Allah, and He is the subject of "subjected" through figurative attribution (al-isnad al-majazi), or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "that," or "it is from Him." The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that He subjected these things as existing from Him and present with Him, since He is their originator by His power and wisdom, then He subjected them to His creation. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also possible that "from Him" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "They all are from Him," and that "and what is in the earth" is the subject, with "from Him" as its predicate. End of quotation. These two possibilities are not permissible except according to the opinion of al-Akhfash, because "jamiʿan" (all) would then be a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and its governing element would be implicit, namely the prepositional phrase. It is thus like "Zayd standing in the house," and it is not permissible according to the position of the majority.

﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive﴾: it was revealed in the early period of Islam. He commanded the believers to pardon the disbelievers and not to punish them for their sins, but rather to bear patiently with them. This was said by al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. It was said: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated). Most scholars hold that it is abrogated (mansukha, subject to naskh, abrogation) by the verse of the sword. Regarding the apocopate form "yaghfirū" (let them forgive), the grammarians have several views, which were discussed under ﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31] in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿Who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾: that is, His events against His enemies and His vengeance upon them. Mujahid said: it is also said that the days are the days of His favour, His help, His bounty in Paradise, and other things. It is also said: they do not hope for the times that Allah appointed for the reward of the believers and their promised success. It was said: it was revealed before the verse of fighting, then its ruling was abrogated. The saying of Ibn ʿAbbas was mentioned earlier, that it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: it was said that a disbelieving man insulted him, so he intended to seize him. The majority read ﴿that Allah may recompense﴾ with the nun (linajziya Allah, "that We may recompense"); Zayd ibn ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Aʿmash, Abu ʿUlayya, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read it with the nun, while Shayba and Abu Jaʿfar, with a variant from him, read it with the ya' in the passive voice (liyujza). This reading is also related from ʿAsim. It contains proof for the one who permits forming the verb in the passive voice so that the prepositional object (majrur), which is "bi-ma," takes the place of the subject, and the explicit direct object, which is "qawman" (a people), is put in the accusative. Its parallel is: "He was struck with a whip, Zayd." The majority do not permit this. This reading is explained as the verb being formed with a verbal noun (maṣdar) as its subject, that is: "let the recompense be recompensed to a people." This too is not permissible according to the majority. However, it is interpreted as being in the accusative by an omitted verb whose estimated form is "He recompenses a people," so there are two clauses: one is "let the recompense be recompensed to a people," and the other is "He recompenses them, a people." Here "qawman" (a people) refers to the forgivers, and it is indefinite to indicate their high status, as if it were said: "a people," meaning a people whose nature is to overlook evil deeds, pardon harms, and bear the hardship. It was also said: they are those who do not hope for the days of Allah, that is, because of the sins they used to earn, as if it were said: "You do not repay them, so that We may repay them."

﴿Whoever does righteousness﴾, like these forgivers, ﴿and whoever does evil﴾, like these disbelievers. The lam appears in ﴿for himself﴾ (falinafsihi), because loves and fortunes are employed for it with ʿalā, which indicates elevation and dominance, as you say: "Affairs are easily accomplished for Zayd and difficult for ʿAmr." ﴿The Book﴾ is the Torah. ﴿The judgment﴾ is decision, and the settling of affairs, because sovereignty was among them. It was said: "judgment" means jurisprudence. It is said: the knowledge of rulings was not as broad for any prophet as it was on the tongue of Musa, and from it the good, delightful and lawful things, and with that the blessing is complete. These were manna and quails, and the good things of al-Sham, which is the blessed land. ﴿Clear proofs﴾, that is, evident indications of the affair, that is, of the revelation by which affairs were distinguished. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "of the affair," that is, of the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that he would emigrate from Tihama to Yathrib. It was said: they are the miracles of Musa.

﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾: its explanation has preceded in Surah al-Shura.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 45, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

Surat al-Jathiyah
(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)
﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain.﴾ ﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and with it gives life to the earth after its death, and in the directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾ ﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in mockery. For those is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿Before them is Hell, and not avail them what they earned, nor what they took as protectors other than Allah. And for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord, for them is a punishment of painful wrath.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail therein by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood, and We provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds.﴾ ﴿And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾.

(p-42) This surah is Meccan; Ibn 'Atiyyah said: without disagreement. Al-Mawardi mentioned that the verse ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ is Medinan, and was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said, and al-Nahhas and al-Mahdawi related from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning 'Umar: a polytheist insulted him in Mecca before the Hijrah, so he wanted to strike him, and then it was revealed. The connection of its beginning with the end of what precedes it is most clear. He (Allah) said: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58], and He said: (Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book), and the discussion of ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ has preceded at the beginning of al-Zumar. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: His saying (al-'Aziz al-Hakim) may be taken as an attribute of Allah, so that is a literal reading; and if we take it as an attribute of the Book, it would be figurative, and the literal is preferable to the figurative, together with the fact that increased proximity necessitates preponderance. End. And this which he hesitated over in his saying "if we take it as an attribute of the Book" is not permissible. If it were an attribute of the Book, it would be adjacent to it, and the construction would be: "the revelation of the Book, the Almighty, the All-Wise, from Allah," because "from Allah" either relates to "revelation," with "revelation" being the predicate of Ha-Mim, or to an elided subject, so it is not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun with it, as in "I was pleased by the striking of Zayd, the whip of the excellent," or in the position of the predicate, with "revelation" being the subject, so it is also not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun, as in "striking Zayd severe the excellent." The correct construction in such cases is for the attribute to be adjacent to its qualified noun.

﴿Indeed in the heavens and the earth﴾: it is possible that it means: in the creation of the heavens, like His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾. The apparent meaning is that it is not intended to restrict to creation, but rather in the heavens and the earth in general and comprehensively, i.e., in whatever you consider of them, of creation or other, of subjection, illumination, and other things. (Signs): He did not present the signs in detail, but presented them in summary, referring to profound matters which thought stirs up and about many of which the Law informs. He made them (for the believers), since within faith is intellect and assent.

﴿And what He disperses of living creatures﴾, i.e., in other than your kind, and it is conjoined to ﴿and in your creation﴾. Whoever permits conjunction to a pronoun in the genitive without repeating the governing preposition permits that ﴿and what He disperses﴾ be conjoined to the pronoun in ﴿in your creation﴾; this is the view of the Kufans, Yunus, and al-Akhfash, and it is the correct view, and it was chosen by the teacher Abu 'Ali al-Shalawbini. Al-Zamakhshari said: conjoining to it is ugly. This is a branch on the view of Sibawayh and the majority of the Basrans. He said: likewise, if they emphasized it, they disliked saying: "I passed by you, you and Zayd." End. This is permitted by al-Jarmi and al-Zibyari in speech. He said: (for a people who are certain): they are those who have a reflection that leads them to certainty.

﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day﴾: the discussion of its like has preceded in surat al-Baqarah. Al-Jumhur read "ayat" as plural in the nominative in both places, while al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read it in the accusative in both places, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read both in the nominative as singular. Ubayy and 'Abd Allah read "la-ayat" in both places, like the first. As for ﴿ayat li-qawmin ya'qilun﴾ in the nominative and accusative, the reading was used as evidence, along with its like from what came in the words of al-Akhfash, by those who follow his view regarding conjoining two governed elements of two governors with "wa"; this is an issue with four views, which we mentioned in (the book al-Tadhyil wa-l-Takmil li-Sharh al-Tashil). As for what concerns this verse: whoever reads "ayat" in the accusative with "wa" conjoins "wa-ikhtilaf" to the genitive after "fi" before it, which is ﴿and in your creation and what He disperses﴾, and conjoins "ayat" to "ayat." Whoever reads it in the nominative does likewise, and the two governors are first "inna" and "fi," and second the inceptive and "fi." Al-Zamakhshari said: "wa" was placed in their stead, so it governed the genitive in "wa-ikhtilafi al-layli wa-l-nahari" and the accusative in "ayat," and when read in the nominative, the governors are the inceptive and "fi," and "wa" governing the nominative is not correct, because the correct view among the positions is that the conjunctive particle does not govern. Whoever prevents conjunction according to al-Akhfash's view holds that the preposition is implied and is estimated. In "ikhtilaf," the governing is for the particle implied, and "wa" took the place of a single governor. What indicates that "fi" is estimated is the reading of 'Abd Allah: "wa-fi ikhtilafi" explicitly, and its being fronted in ﴿and in your creation﴾ made its omission acceptable. The accusative of "ayat" was also explained as an emphasis on the preceding "ayat," and as the implied particle "fi." It was also read "wa-ikhtilafun" in the nominative as the predicate of an elided subject, i.e., "they are signs," and also with an implied particle. And he read: "wa-ikhtilafu al-layli wa-l-nahari ayatun," with "ikhtilafu" in the nominative and "ayatun" singular, and likewise ﴿wa-ma yabuththu min dabbatin﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali, Talhah, and 'Isa read ﴿wa-tasrifi al-riyah﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that the fair-minded among the servants, when they look at the heavens and the earth with correct observation, know that they are made, and that they necessarily have a maker, so they believe in Allah and affirm. When they look at the creation of themselves and their movement from state to state and form to form, and at the creation of what is on the surface of the earth of the kinds of animals, they increase in faith, attain certainty, and doubt is removed from them. When they look at the other events that renew at every time, such as the alternation of night and day, the descent of rain, the earth's life after its death by it, and the directing of winds south and north, east and west, they reason, their knowledge is firmly established, and their certainty becomes pure. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He mentioned eight proofs in al-Baqarah, and here six; he did not mention the ship and the cloud. The reason for that is that the movement of the ship and the cloud depends on the differing winds, so he mentioned the winds. There he made the end of the eight one, and here he arranged them in three endings: "they believe," "they are certain," "they reason." He said: I think the reason for this arrangement is: "if you are believers" (cf. al-Baqarah), so understand these proofs; if you are not believers nor certain, then at least be among the reasoners; so strive. There he said: "Indeed in the creation of the heavens," and here: "in the heavens," which shows that the creation is other than the created, which is the correct view according to our companions; and there is no difference between saying "in the heavens" and "in the creation of the heavens." End. And in it is abridgement, anteposition and postposition.

﴿These are the verses of Allah﴾: i.e., these verses, which are the proofs mentioned. (We recite them): i.e., we narrate them to you, associated with truth. We recite them in the position of the circumstantial, i.e., recited. Al-Zamakhshari said: The governing element is what "these" indicates of the meaning of pointing and the like, and this is "ba'li shaykhan" (my husband being an old man). End. It is not like it, because "fi" and "hadha" have a particle of alerting. It was said: the governing element of the circumstantial is what the particle of alerting indicates, i.e., "be alert." As for "tilka," there is no particle of alerting in it that governs by the meaning of alerting, since the particle may govern the circumstantial: "be alert to Zayd in the state of his shaykh-hood and in the state of his standing." It was said: the governing element in such a construction is an elided verb indicated by the meaning, i.e., "look at him in the state of his shaykh-hood," so the demonstrative is not the governor nor the particle of alerting, if there is one there. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "We recite them" contains an elided noun, i.e., we recite its matter and explain the lesson in it. It may be that by "verses of Allah" is meant the Qur'an revealed with these meanings, so there is no elided noun in "we recite them." End. "We recite them" means: the King orders that we recite them. It was read "yatluwha" with the third person, referring to Allah. "Bil-haqq": with truth, because its soundness is known by rational proofs.

﴿Then in what statement﴾ the verse: it contains rebuke, reproach and threat. (After Allah): i.e., after the statement of Allah, which is His Book and His speech, like His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book similar in its parts﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and He said: (p-44) ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], i.e., after the statement of Allah and His speech. Al-Dahhak said: after the monotheism of Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: "after Allah and His verses," i.e., after the verses of Allah, like their saying: "Zayd pleased me and his generosity," meaning: "the generosity of Zayd pleased me." End. This is nothing, because in terms of meaning it involves inserting nouns without necessity, and conjunction, while the intended meaning is other than conjunction, bringing it into the category of apposition, since the estimate "the generosity of Zayd" applies only to "Zayd pleased me, his generosity," without "wa," as apposition; and this is a reversal of the realities of grammar. Rather, the meaning of "Zayd pleased me and his generosity" is that Zayd's person pleased him and his generosity pleased him, so they are two pleasures, not one pleasure; and we have already responded to his like of this saying previously. Abu Ja'far, al-A'raj, Shaybah, Qatadah, the two Harami, Abu 'Amr, and 'Asim in one transmission read "yu'minun" with the third person by yaa'; al-A'mash and the rest of the seven read it with the second person by ta' of address; Talhah read "tuqinun" with ta' on top and qaf from iqan.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, and it was said: concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and what he used to buy of the stories of non-Arabs and occupy people with them instead of listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general concerning whoever harms the religion of Allah. "Affak" and "athim" are intensive adjectives; the discussion of the words of this verse has preceded. Al-Jumhur read "'alima," and Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq read it with a damma on the 'ayn and shadda on the lam, passive, meaning: "he came to know." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the meaning of "thumma" in His saying ﴿then persists﴾? I say: its meaning is like its meaning in the saying of the speaker:
"He sees the surges of death, then visits them,"
because the surges of death are of the sort that the one who sees them should escape by himself and seek flight from them; as for visiting them and advancing to engage with them, this is something far-fetched. So the meaning of "thumma" is the indication that the act of advancing upon them after seeing them and witnessing them is something that is deemed unlikely by custom and nature. Likewise the clear and decisive signs of Allah which are established by truth: whoever has them recited to him and hears them, his persistence in error in their presence and his arrogance against believing in them is deemed unlikely by the intellects.

(p-٤٥)

﴿He took them in mockery﴾. He did not say "took it," indicating that when he perceives any part of the speech to be among the verses that Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), he plunges into mocking all the verses, and does not restrict his mockery to what has reached him. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And when he learns something of Our verses﴾ means that the obstinate person can seize upon it and make it a pretext by which he climbs to slander and defamation. He fabricates it and takes the verses of Allah in mockery. This is like Ibn al-Zib'ara's fabrication of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], and his sophistry toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "I have defeated you." The pronoun may also refer to a thing, because it carries the meaning of the verse, like the saying of Abu al-Atahiya:

"My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the Guided Upright One suffice for it,"

where he meant ʿUtba. End of quotation. ʿUtba was a slave girl whom Abu al-Atahiya loved and to whom he was attached.

The demonstrative ﴿those﴾ refers to every liar, because it encompasses the liars. It is first treated according to the wording of "kull" (every), then it is put in the singular according to meaning and then in the plural, like His saying: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoices﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53].

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾: that is, before them. "Waraʾ" means what is hidden from behind and in front.

﴿Nor will what they earned avail them anything﴾ of wealth in their trade, ﴿nor what they took as protectors besides Allah﴾ of idols. ﴿This﴾, that is the Qur'an, ﴿is guidance﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in guidance, like your saying: "This is a man," meaning he is complete in manhood. Talha, Ibn Muhaysin, the people of Makkah, Ibn Kathir and Hafs read ﴿painful﴾ in the nominative as an adjective of ʿadhab (punishment). Al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, ʿIsa, al-Aʿmash and the rest of the seven read it in the genitive as an adjective of rijz (torment).

﴿Allah is He who subjected﴾, the verse: it is a verse of reflection on the subjection of this great creation and the ships that run in it, by this lowly creation, which is the human being. ﴿By His command﴾: that is, by His power. He put the command in the place of power, as if He commands the ships to run. ﴿From His bounty﴾ through trade, diving for pearls and coral, and extracting fresh flesh. ﴿What is in the heavens﴾ of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, winds and air, and the angels entrusted with all of this. ﴿And what is in the earth﴾ of animals, waters, mountains and plants.

The majority read ﴿from Him﴾ (minhu). Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a kasra on the mim, a shadda on the nun, and a fatha on the ta' (tā'), as a verbal noun (maṣdar). Abu Hatim said: attributing this reading to Ibn ʿAbbas is an injustice. Abu al-Fath related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, al-Jahdari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and Sahib al-Lawamih also related it from these four. Ibn Khalawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Salama ibn Muharib read likewise, except that he put a damma on the ta', meaning "He is from Him." He also read with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the nun. The pronoun of attribution refers to Allah, and He is the subject of "subjected" through figurative attribution (al-isnad al-majazi), or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "that," or "it is from Him." The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that He subjected these things as existing from Him and present with Him, since He is their originator by His power and wisdom, then He subjected them to His creation. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also possible that "from Him" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "They all are from Him," and that "and what is in the earth" is the subject, with "from Him" as its predicate. End of quotation. These two possibilities are not permissible except according to the opinion of al-Akhfash, because "jamiʿan" (all) would then be a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and its governing element would be implicit, namely the prepositional phrase. It is thus like "Zayd standing in the house," and it is not permissible according to the position of the majority.

﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive﴾: it was revealed in the early period of Islam. He commanded the believers to pardon the disbelievers and not to punish them for their sins, but rather to bear patiently with them. This was said by al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. It was said: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated). Most scholars hold that it is abrogated (mansukha, subject to naskh, abrogation) by the verse of the sword. Regarding the apocopate form "yaghfirū" (let them forgive), the grammarians have several views, which were discussed under ﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31] in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿Who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾: that is, His events against His enemies and His vengeance upon them. Mujahid said: it is also said that the days are the days of His favour, His help, His bounty in Paradise, and other things. It is also said: they do not hope for the times that Allah appointed for the reward of the believers and their promised success. It was said: it was revealed before the verse of fighting, then its ruling was abrogated. The saying of Ibn ʿAbbas was mentioned earlier, that it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: it was said that a disbelieving man insulted him, so he intended to seize him. The majority read ﴿that Allah may recompense﴾ with the nun (linajziya Allah, "that We may recompense"); Zayd ibn ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Aʿmash, Abu ʿUlayya, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read it with the nun, while Shayba and Abu Jaʿfar, with a variant from him, read it with the ya' in the passive voice (liyujza). This reading is also related from ʿAsim. It contains proof for the one who permits forming the verb in the passive voice so that the prepositional object (majrur), which is "bi-ma," takes the place of the subject, and the explicit direct object, which is "qawman" (a people), is put in the accusative. Its parallel is: "He was struck with a whip, Zayd." The majority do not permit this. This reading is explained as the verb being formed with a verbal noun (maṣdar) as its subject, that is: "let the recompense be recompensed to a people." This too is not permissible according to the majority. However, it is interpreted as being in the accusative by an omitted verb whose estimated form is "He recompenses a people," so there are two clauses: one is "let the recompense be recompensed to a people," and the other is "He recompenses them, a people." Here "qawman" (a people) refers to the forgivers, and it is indefinite to indicate their high status, as if it were said: "a people," meaning a people whose nature is to overlook evil deeds, pardon harms, and bear the hardship. It was also said: they are those who do not hope for the days of Allah, that is, because of the sins they used to earn, as if it were said: "You do not repay them, so that We may repay them."

﴿Whoever does righteousness﴾, like these forgivers, ﴿and whoever does evil﴾, like these disbelievers. The lam appears in ﴿for himself﴾ (falinafsihi), because loves and fortunes are employed for it with ʿalā, which indicates elevation and dominance, as you say: "Affairs are easily accomplished for Zayd and difficult for ʿAmr." ﴿The Book﴾ is the Torah. ﴿The judgment﴾ is decision, and the settling of affairs, because sovereignty was among them. It was said: "judgment" means jurisprudence. It is said: the knowledge of rulings was not as broad for any prophet as it was on the tongue of Musa, and from it the good, delightful and lawful things, and with that the blessing is complete. These were manna and quails, and the good things of al-Sham, which is the blessed land. ﴿Clear proofs﴾, that is, evident indications of the affair, that is, of the revelation by which affairs were distinguished. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "of the affair," that is, of the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that he would emigrate from Tihama to Yathrib. It was said: they are the miracles of Musa.

﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾: its explanation has preceded in Surah al-Shura.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 45, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

Surat al-Jathiyah
(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)
﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain.﴾ ﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and with it gives life to the earth after its death, and in the directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾ ﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in mockery. For those is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿Before them is Hell, and not avail them what they earned, nor what they took as protectors other than Allah. And for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord, for them is a punishment of painful wrath.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail therein by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood, and We provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds.﴾ ﴿And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾.

(p-42) This surah is Meccan; Ibn 'Atiyyah said: without disagreement. Al-Mawardi mentioned that the verse ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ is Medinan, and was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said, and al-Nahhas and al-Mahdawi related from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning 'Umar: a polytheist insulted him in Mecca before the Hijrah, so he wanted to strike him, and then it was revealed. The connection of its beginning with the end of what precedes it is most clear. He (Allah) said: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58], and He said: (Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book), and the discussion of ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ has preceded at the beginning of al-Zumar. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: His saying (al-'Aziz al-Hakim) may be taken as an attribute of Allah, so that is a literal reading; and if we take it as an attribute of the Book, it would be figurative, and the literal is preferable to the figurative, together with the fact that increased proximity necessitates preponderance. End. And this which he hesitated over in his saying "if we take it as an attribute of the Book" is not permissible. If it were an attribute of the Book, it would be adjacent to it, and the construction would be: "the revelation of the Book, the Almighty, the All-Wise, from Allah," because "from Allah" either relates to "revelation," with "revelation" being the predicate of Ha-Mim, or to an elided subject, so it is not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun with it, as in "I was pleased by the striking of Zayd, the whip of the excellent," or in the position of the predicate, with "revelation" being the subject, so it is also not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun, as in "striking Zayd severe the excellent." The correct construction in such cases is for the attribute to be adjacent to its qualified noun.

﴿Indeed in the heavens and the earth﴾: it is possible that it means: in the creation of the heavens, like His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾. The apparent meaning is that it is not intended to restrict to creation, but rather in the heavens and the earth in general and comprehensively, i.e., in whatever you consider of them, of creation or other, of subjection, illumination, and other things. (Signs): He did not present the signs in detail, but presented them in summary, referring to profound matters which thought stirs up and about many of which the Law informs. He made them (for the believers), since within faith is intellect and assent.

﴿And what He disperses of living creatures﴾, i.e., in other than your kind, and it is conjoined to ﴿and in your creation﴾. Whoever permits conjunction to a pronoun in the genitive without repeating the governing preposition permits that ﴿and what He disperses﴾ be conjoined to the pronoun in ﴿in your creation﴾; this is the view of the Kufans, Yunus, and al-Akhfash, and it is the correct view, and it was chosen by the teacher Abu 'Ali al-Shalawbini. Al-Zamakhshari said: conjoining to it is ugly. This is a branch on the view of Sibawayh and the majority of the Basrans. He said: likewise, if they emphasized it, they disliked saying: "I passed by you, you and Zayd." End. This is permitted by al-Jarmi and al-Zibyari in speech. He said: (for a people who are certain): they are those who have a reflection that leads them to certainty.

﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day﴾: the discussion of its like has preceded in surat al-Baqarah. Al-Jumhur read "ayat" as plural in the nominative in both places, while al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read it in the accusative in both places, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read both in the nominative as singular. Ubayy and 'Abd Allah read "la-ayat" in both places, like the first. As for ﴿ayat li-qawmin ya'qilun﴾ in the nominative and accusative, the reading was used as evidence, along with its like from what came in the words of al-Akhfash, by those who follow his view regarding conjoining two governed elements of two governors with "wa"; this is an issue with four views, which we mentioned in (the book al-Tadhyil wa-l-Takmil li-Sharh al-Tashil). As for what concerns this verse: whoever reads "ayat" in the accusative with "wa" conjoins "wa-ikhtilaf" to the genitive after "fi" before it, which is ﴿and in your creation and what He disperses﴾, and conjoins "ayat" to "ayat." Whoever reads it in the nominative does likewise, and the two governors are first "inna" and "fi," and second the inceptive and "fi." Al-Zamakhshari said: "wa" was placed in their stead, so it governed the genitive in "wa-ikhtilafi al-layli wa-l-nahari" and the accusative in "ayat," and when read in the nominative, the governors are the inceptive and "fi," and "wa" governing the nominative is not correct, because the correct view among the positions is that the conjunctive particle does not govern. Whoever prevents conjunction according to al-Akhfash's view holds that the preposition is implied and is estimated. In "ikhtilaf," the governing is for the particle implied, and "wa" took the place of a single governor. What indicates that "fi" is estimated is the reading of 'Abd Allah: "wa-fi ikhtilafi" explicitly, and its being fronted in ﴿and in your creation﴾ made its omission acceptable. The accusative of "ayat" was also explained as an emphasis on the preceding "ayat," and as the implied particle "fi." It was also read "wa-ikhtilafun" in the nominative as the predicate of an elided subject, i.e., "they are signs," and also with an implied particle. And he read: "wa-ikhtilafu al-layli wa-l-nahari ayatun," with "ikhtilafu" in the nominative and "ayatun" singular, and likewise ﴿wa-ma yabuththu min dabbatin﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali, Talhah, and 'Isa read ﴿wa-tasrifi al-riyah﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that the fair-minded among the servants, when they look at the heavens and the earth with correct observation, know that they are made, and that they necessarily have a maker, so they believe in Allah and affirm. When they look at the creation of themselves and their movement from state to state and form to form, and at the creation of what is on the surface of the earth of the kinds of animals, they increase in faith, attain certainty, and doubt is removed from them. When they look at the other events that renew at every time, such as the alternation of night and day, the descent of rain, the earth's life after its death by it, and the directing of winds south and north, east and west, they reason, their knowledge is firmly established, and their certainty becomes pure. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He mentioned eight proofs in al-Baqarah, and here six; he did not mention the ship and the cloud. The reason for that is that the movement of the ship and the cloud depends on the differing winds, so he mentioned the winds. There he made the end of the eight one, and here he arranged them in three endings: "they believe," "they are certain," "they reason." He said: I think the reason for this arrangement is: "if you are believers" (cf. al-Baqarah), so understand these proofs; if you are not believers nor certain, then at least be among the reasoners; so strive. There he said: "Indeed in the creation of the heavens," and here: "in the heavens," which shows that the creation is other than the created, which is the correct view according to our companions; and there is no difference between saying "in the heavens" and "in the creation of the heavens." End. And in it is abridgement, anteposition and postposition.

﴿These are the verses of Allah﴾: i.e., these verses, which are the proofs mentioned. (We recite them): i.e., we narrate them to you, associated with truth. We recite them in the position of the circumstantial, i.e., recited. Al-Zamakhshari said: The governing element is what "these" indicates of the meaning of pointing and the like, and this is "ba'li shaykhan" (my husband being an old man). End. It is not like it, because "fi" and "hadha" have a particle of alerting. It was said: the governing element of the circumstantial is what the particle of alerting indicates, i.e., "be alert." As for "tilka," there is no particle of alerting in it that governs by the meaning of alerting, since the particle may govern the circumstantial: "be alert to Zayd in the state of his shaykh-hood and in the state of his standing." It was said: the governing element in such a construction is an elided verb indicated by the meaning, i.e., "look at him in the state of his shaykh-hood," so the demonstrative is not the governor nor the particle of alerting, if there is one there. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "We recite them" contains an elided noun, i.e., we recite its matter and explain the lesson in it. It may be that by "verses of Allah" is meant the Qur'an revealed with these meanings, so there is no elided noun in "we recite them." End. "We recite them" means: the King orders that we recite them. It was read "yatluwha" with the third person, referring to Allah. "Bil-haqq": with truth, because its soundness is known by rational proofs.

﴿Then in what statement﴾ the verse: it contains rebuke, reproach and threat. (After Allah): i.e., after the statement of Allah, which is His Book and His speech, like His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book similar in its parts﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and He said: (p-44) ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], i.e., after the statement of Allah and His speech. Al-Dahhak said: after the monotheism of Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: "after Allah and His verses," i.e., after the verses of Allah, like their saying: "Zayd pleased me and his generosity," meaning: "the generosity of Zayd pleased me." End. This is nothing, because in terms of meaning it involves inserting nouns without necessity, and conjunction, while the intended meaning is other than conjunction, bringing it into the category of apposition, since the estimate "the generosity of Zayd" applies only to "Zayd pleased me, his generosity," without "wa," as apposition; and this is a reversal of the realities of grammar. Rather, the meaning of "Zayd pleased me and his generosity" is that Zayd's person pleased him and his generosity pleased him, so they are two pleasures, not one pleasure; and we have already responded to his like of this saying previously. Abu Ja'far, al-A'raj, Shaybah, Qatadah, the two Harami, Abu 'Amr, and 'Asim in one transmission read "yu'minun" with the third person by yaa'; al-A'mash and the rest of the seven read it with the second person by ta' of address; Talhah read "tuqinun" with ta' on top and qaf from iqan.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, and it was said: concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and what he used to buy of the stories of non-Arabs and occupy people with them instead of listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general concerning whoever harms the religion of Allah. "Affak" and "athim" are intensive adjectives; the discussion of the words of this verse has preceded. Al-Jumhur read "'alima," and Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq read it with a damma on the 'ayn and shadda on the lam, passive, meaning: "he came to know." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the meaning of "thumma" in His saying ﴿then persists﴾? I say: its meaning is like its meaning in the saying of the speaker:
"He sees the surges of death, then visits them,"
because the surges of death are of the sort that the one who sees them should escape by himself and seek flight from them; as for visiting them and advancing to engage with them, this is something far-fetched. So the meaning of "thumma" is the indication that the act of advancing upon them after seeing them and witnessing them is something that is deemed unlikely by custom and nature. Likewise the clear and decisive signs of Allah which are established by truth: whoever has them recited to him and hears them, his persistence in error in their presence and his arrogance against believing in them is deemed unlikely by the intellects.

(p-٤٥)

﴿He took them in mockery﴾. He did not say "took it," indicating that when he perceives any part of the speech to be among the verses that Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), he plunges into mocking all the verses, and does not restrict his mockery to what has reached him. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And when he learns something of Our verses﴾ means that the obstinate person can seize upon it and make it a pretext by which he climbs to slander and defamation. He fabricates it and takes the verses of Allah in mockery. This is like Ibn al-Zib'ara's fabrication of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], and his sophistry toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "I have defeated you." The pronoun may also refer to a thing, because it carries the meaning of the verse, like the saying of Abu al-Atahiya:

"My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the Guided Upright One suffice for it,"

where he meant ʿUtba. End of quotation. ʿUtba was a slave girl whom Abu al-Atahiya loved and to whom he was attached.

The demonstrative ﴿those﴾ refers to every liar, because it encompasses the liars. It is first treated according to the wording of "kull" (every), then it is put in the singular according to meaning and then in the plural, like His saying: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoices﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53].

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾: that is, before them. "Waraʾ" means what is hidden from behind and in front.

﴿Nor will what they earned avail them anything﴾ of wealth in their trade, ﴿nor what they took as protectors besides Allah﴾ of idols. ﴿This﴾, that is the Qur'an, ﴿is guidance﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in guidance, like your saying: "This is a man," meaning he is complete in manhood. Talha, Ibn Muhaysin, the people of Makkah, Ibn Kathir and Hafs read ﴿painful﴾ in the nominative as an adjective of ʿadhab (punishment). Al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, ʿIsa, al-Aʿmash and the rest of the seven read it in the genitive as an adjective of rijz (torment).

﴿Allah is He who subjected﴾, the verse: it is a verse of reflection on the subjection of this great creation and the ships that run in it, by this lowly creation, which is the human being. ﴿By His command﴾: that is, by His power. He put the command in the place of power, as if He commands the ships to run. ﴿From His bounty﴾ through trade, diving for pearls and coral, and extracting fresh flesh. ﴿What is in the heavens﴾ of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, winds and air, and the angels entrusted with all of this. ﴿And what is in the earth﴾ of animals, waters, mountains and plants.

The majority read ﴿from Him﴾ (minhu). Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a kasra on the mim, a shadda on the nun, and a fatha on the ta' (tā'), as a verbal noun (maṣdar). Abu Hatim said: attributing this reading to Ibn ʿAbbas is an injustice. Abu al-Fath related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, al-Jahdari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and Sahib al-Lawamih also related it from these four. Ibn Khalawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Salama ibn Muharib read likewise, except that he put a damma on the ta', meaning "He is from Him." He also read with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the nun. The pronoun of attribution refers to Allah, and He is the subject of "subjected" through figurative attribution (al-isnad al-majazi), or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "that," or "it is from Him." The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that He subjected these things as existing from Him and present with Him, since He is their originator by His power and wisdom, then He subjected them to His creation. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also possible that "from Him" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "They all are from Him," and that "and what is in the earth" is the subject, with "from Him" as its predicate. End of quotation. These two possibilities are not permissible except according to the opinion of al-Akhfash, because "jamiʿan" (all) would then be a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and its governing element would be implicit, namely the prepositional phrase. It is thus like "Zayd standing in the house," and it is not permissible according to the position of the majority.

﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive﴾: it was revealed in the early period of Islam. He commanded the believers to pardon the disbelievers and not to punish them for their sins, but rather to bear patiently with them. This was said by al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. It was said: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated). Most scholars hold that it is abrogated (mansukha, subject to naskh, abrogation) by the verse of the sword. Regarding the apocopate form "yaghfirū" (let them forgive), the grammarians have several views, which were discussed under ﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31] in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿Who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾: that is, His events against His enemies and His vengeance upon them. Mujahid said: it is also said that the days are the days of His favour, His help, His bounty in Paradise, and other things. It is also said: they do not hope for the times that Allah appointed for the reward of the believers and their promised success. It was said: it was revealed before the verse of fighting, then its ruling was abrogated. The saying of Ibn ʿAbbas was mentioned earlier, that it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: it was said that a disbelieving man insulted him, so he intended to seize him. The majority read ﴿that Allah may recompense﴾ with the nun (linajziya Allah, "that We may recompense"); Zayd ibn ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Aʿmash, Abu ʿUlayya, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read it with the nun, while Shayba and Abu Jaʿfar, with a variant from him, read it with the ya' in the passive voice (liyujza). This reading is also related from ʿAsim. It contains proof for the one who permits forming the verb in the passive voice so that the prepositional object (majrur), which is "bi-ma," takes the place of the subject, and the explicit direct object, which is "qawman" (a people), is put in the accusative. Its parallel is: "He was struck with a whip, Zayd." The majority do not permit this. This reading is explained as the verb being formed with a verbal noun (maṣdar) as its subject, that is: "let the recompense be recompensed to a people." This too is not permissible according to the majority. However, it is interpreted as being in the accusative by an omitted verb whose estimated form is "He recompenses a people," so there are two clauses: one is "let the recompense be recompensed to a people," and the other is "He recompenses them, a people." Here "qawman" (a people) refers to the forgivers, and it is indefinite to indicate their high status, as if it were said: "a people," meaning a people whose nature is to overlook evil deeds, pardon harms, and bear the hardship. It was also said: they are those who do not hope for the days of Allah, that is, because of the sins they used to earn, as if it were said: "You do not repay them, so that We may repay them."

﴿Whoever does righteousness﴾, like these forgivers, ﴿and whoever does evil﴾, like these disbelievers. The lam appears in ﴿for himself﴾ (falinafsihi), because loves and fortunes are employed for it with ʿalā, which indicates elevation and dominance, as you say: "Affairs are easily accomplished for Zayd and difficult for ʿAmr." ﴿The Book﴾ is the Torah. ﴿The judgment﴾ is decision, and the settling of affairs, because sovereignty was among them. It was said: "judgment" means jurisprudence. It is said: the knowledge of rulings was not as broad for any prophet as it was on the tongue of Musa, and from it the good, delightful and lawful things, and with that the blessing is complete. These were manna and quails, and the good things of al-Sham, which is the blessed land. ﴿Clear proofs﴾, that is, evident indications of the affair, that is, of the revelation by which affairs were distinguished. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "of the affair," that is, of the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that he would emigrate from Tihama to Yathrib. It was said: they are the miracles of Musa.

﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾: its explanation has preceded in Surah al-Shura.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 45, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

Surat al-Jathiyah
(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)
﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain.﴾ ﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and with it gives life to the earth after its death, and in the directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾ ﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in mockery. For those is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿Before them is Hell, and not avail them what they earned, nor what they took as protectors other than Allah. And for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord, for them is a punishment of painful wrath.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail therein by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood, and We provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds.﴾ ﴿And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾.

(p-42) This surah is Meccan; Ibn 'Atiyyah said: without disagreement. Al-Mawardi mentioned that the verse ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ is Medinan, and was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said, and al-Nahhas and al-Mahdawi related from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning 'Umar: a polytheist insulted him in Mecca before the Hijrah, so he wanted to strike him, and then it was revealed. The connection of its beginning with the end of what precedes it is most clear. He (Allah) said: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58], and He said: (Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book), and the discussion of ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ has preceded at the beginning of al-Zumar. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: His saying (al-'Aziz al-Hakim) may be taken as an attribute of Allah, so that is a literal reading; and if we take it as an attribute of the Book, it would be figurative, and the literal is preferable to the figurative, together with the fact that increased proximity necessitates preponderance. End. And this which he hesitated over in his saying "if we take it as an attribute of the Book" is not permissible. If it were an attribute of the Book, it would be adjacent to it, and the construction would be: "the revelation of the Book, the Almighty, the All-Wise, from Allah," because "from Allah" either relates to "revelation," with "revelation" being the predicate of Ha-Mim, or to an elided subject, so it is not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun with it, as in "I was pleased by the striking of Zayd, the whip of the excellent," or in the position of the predicate, with "revelation" being the subject, so it is also not permissible to separate the attribute from the qualified noun, as in "striking Zayd severe the excellent." The correct construction in such cases is for the attribute to be adjacent to its qualified noun.

﴿Indeed in the heavens and the earth﴾: it is possible that it means: in the creation of the heavens, like His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾. The apparent meaning is that it is not intended to restrict to creation, but rather in the heavens and the earth in general and comprehensively, i.e., in whatever you consider of them, of creation or other, of subjection, illumination, and other things. (Signs): He did not present the signs in detail, but presented them in summary, referring to profound matters which thought stirs up and about many of which the Law informs. He made them (for the believers), since within faith is intellect and assent.

﴿And what He disperses of living creatures﴾, i.e., in other than your kind, and it is conjoined to ﴿and in your creation﴾. Whoever permits conjunction to a pronoun in the genitive without repeating the governing preposition permits that ﴿and what He disperses﴾ be conjoined to the pronoun in ﴿in your creation﴾; this is the view of the Kufans, Yunus, and al-Akhfash, and it is the correct view, and it was chosen by the teacher Abu 'Ali al-Shalawbini. Al-Zamakhshari said: conjoining to it is ugly. This is a branch on the view of Sibawayh and the majority of the Basrans. He said: likewise, if they emphasized it, they disliked saying: "I passed by you, you and Zayd." End. This is permitted by al-Jarmi and al-Zibyari in speech. He said: (for a people who are certain): they are those who have a reflection that leads them to certainty.

﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day﴾: the discussion of its like has preceded in surat al-Baqarah. Al-Jumhur read "ayat" as plural in the nominative in both places, while al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read it in the accusative in both places, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read both in the nominative as singular. Ubayy and 'Abd Allah read "la-ayat" in both places, like the first. As for ﴿ayat li-qawmin ya'qilun﴾ in the nominative and accusative, the reading was used as evidence, along with its like from what came in the words of al-Akhfash, by those who follow his view regarding conjoining two governed elements of two governors with "wa"; this is an issue with four views, which we mentioned in (the book al-Tadhyil wa-l-Takmil li-Sharh al-Tashil). As for what concerns this verse: whoever reads "ayat" in the accusative with "wa" conjoins "wa-ikhtilaf" to the genitive after "fi" before it, which is ﴿and in your creation and what He disperses﴾, and conjoins "ayat" to "ayat." Whoever reads it in the nominative does likewise, and the two governors are first "inna" and "fi," and second the inceptive and "fi." Al-Zamakhshari said: "wa" was placed in their stead, so it governed the genitive in "wa-ikhtilafi al-layli wa-l-nahari" and the accusative in "ayat," and when read in the nominative, the governors are the inceptive and "fi," and "wa" governing the nominative is not correct, because the correct view among the positions is that the conjunctive particle does not govern. Whoever prevents conjunction according to al-Akhfash's view holds that the preposition is implied and is estimated. In "ikhtilaf," the governing is for the particle implied, and "wa" took the place of a single governor. What indicates that "fi" is estimated is the reading of 'Abd Allah: "wa-fi ikhtilafi" explicitly, and its being fronted in ﴿and in your creation﴾ made its omission acceptable. The accusative of "ayat" was also explained as an emphasis on the preceding "ayat," and as the implied particle "fi." It was also read "wa-ikhtilafun" in the nominative as the predicate of an elided subject, i.e., "they are signs," and also with an implied particle. And he read: "wa-ikhtilafu al-layli wa-l-nahari ayatun," with "ikhtilafu" in the nominative and "ayatun" singular, and likewise ﴿wa-ma yabuththu min dabbatin﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali, Talhah, and 'Isa read ﴿wa-tasrifi al-riyah﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that the fair-minded among the servants, when they look at the heavens and the earth with correct observation, know that they are made, and that they necessarily have a maker, so they believe in Allah and affirm. When they look at the creation of themselves and their movement from state to state and form to form, and at the creation of what is on the surface of the earth of the kinds of animals, they increase in faith, attain certainty, and doubt is removed from them. When they look at the other events that renew at every time, such as the alternation of night and day, the descent of rain, the earth's life after its death by it, and the directing of winds south and north, east and west, they reason, their knowledge is firmly established, and their certainty becomes pure. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He mentioned eight proofs in al-Baqarah, and here six; he did not mention the ship and the cloud. The reason for that is that the movement of the ship and the cloud depends on the differing winds, so he mentioned the winds. There he made the end of the eight one, and here he arranged them in three endings: "they believe," "they are certain," "they reason." He said: I think the reason for this arrangement is: "if you are believers" (cf. al-Baqarah), so understand these proofs; if you are not believers nor certain, then at least be among the reasoners; so strive. There he said: "Indeed in the creation of the heavens," and here: "in the heavens," which shows that the creation is other than the created, which is the correct view according to our companions; and there is no difference between saying "in the heavens" and "in the creation of the heavens." End. And in it is abridgement, anteposition and postposition.

﴿These are the verses of Allah﴾: i.e., these verses, which are the proofs mentioned. (We recite them): i.e., we narrate them to you, associated with truth. We recite them in the position of the circumstantial, i.e., recited. Al-Zamakhshari said: The governing element is what "these" indicates of the meaning of pointing and the like, and this is "ba'li shaykhan" (my husband being an old man). End. It is not like it, because "fi" and "hadha" have a particle of alerting. It was said: the governing element of the circumstantial is what the particle of alerting indicates, i.e., "be alert." As for "tilka," there is no particle of alerting in it that governs by the meaning of alerting, since the particle may govern the circumstantial: "be alert to Zayd in the state of his shaykh-hood and in the state of his standing." It was said: the governing element in such a construction is an elided verb indicated by the meaning, i.e., "look at him in the state of his shaykh-hood," so the demonstrative is not the governor nor the particle of alerting, if there is one there. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "We recite them" contains an elided noun, i.e., we recite its matter and explain the lesson in it. It may be that by "verses of Allah" is meant the Qur'an revealed with these meanings, so there is no elided noun in "we recite them." End. "We recite them" means: the King orders that we recite them. It was read "yatluwha" with the third person, referring to Allah. "Bil-haqq": with truth, because its soundness is known by rational proofs.

﴿Then in what statement﴾ the verse: it contains rebuke, reproach and threat. (After Allah): i.e., after the statement of Allah, which is His Book and His speech, like His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book similar in its parts﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and He said: (p-44) ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], i.e., after the statement of Allah and His speech. Al-Dahhak said: after the monotheism of Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: "after Allah and His verses," i.e., after the verses of Allah, like their saying: "Zayd pleased me and his generosity," meaning: "the generosity of Zayd pleased me." End. This is nothing, because in terms of meaning it involves inserting nouns without necessity, and conjunction, while the intended meaning is other than conjunction, bringing it into the category of apposition, since the estimate "the generosity of Zayd" applies only to "Zayd pleased me, his generosity," without "wa," as apposition; and this is a reversal of the realities of grammar. Rather, the meaning of "Zayd pleased me and his generosity" is that Zayd's person pleased him and his generosity pleased him, so they are two pleasures, not one pleasure; and we have already responded to his like of this saying previously. Abu Ja'far, al-A'raj, Shaybah, Qatadah, the two Harami, Abu 'Amr, and 'Asim in one transmission read "yu'minun" with the third person by yaa'; al-A'mash and the rest of the seven read it with the second person by ta' of address; Talhah read "tuqinun" with ta' on top and qaf from iqan.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, and it was said: concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and what he used to buy of the stories of non-Arabs and occupy people with them instead of listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general concerning whoever harms the religion of Allah. "Affak" and "athim" are intensive adjectives; the discussion of the words of this verse has preceded. Al-Jumhur read "'alima," and Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq read it with a damma on the 'ayn and shadda on the lam, passive, meaning: "he came to know." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the meaning of "thumma" in His saying ﴿then persists﴾? I say: its meaning is like its meaning in the saying of the speaker:
"He sees the surges of death, then visits them,"
because the surges of death are of the sort that the one who sees them should escape by himself and seek flight from them; as for visiting them and advancing to engage with them, this is something far-fetched. So the meaning of "thumma" is the indication that the act of advancing upon them after seeing them and witnessing them is something that is deemed unlikely by custom and nature. Likewise the clear and decisive signs of Allah which are established by truth: whoever has them recited to him and hears them, his persistence in error in their presence and his arrogance against believing in them is deemed unlikely by the intellects.

(p-٤٥)

﴿He took them in mockery﴾. He did not say "took it," indicating that when he perceives any part of the speech to be among the verses that Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), he plunges into mocking all the verses, and does not restrict his mockery to what has reached him. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And when he learns something of Our verses﴾ means that the obstinate person can seize upon it and make it a pretext by which he climbs to slander and defamation. He fabricates it and takes the verses of Allah in mockery. This is like Ibn al-Zib'ara's fabrication of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], and his sophistry toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "I have defeated you." The pronoun may also refer to a thing, because it carries the meaning of the verse, like the saying of Abu al-Atahiya:

"My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the Guided Upright One suffice for it,"

where he meant ʿUtba. End of quotation. ʿUtba was a slave girl whom Abu al-Atahiya loved and to whom he was attached.

The demonstrative ﴿those﴾ refers to every liar, because it encompasses the liars. It is first treated according to the wording of "kull" (every), then it is put in the singular according to meaning and then in the plural, like His saying: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoices﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53].

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾: that is, before them. "Waraʾ" means what is hidden from behind and in front.

﴿Nor will what they earned avail them anything﴾ of wealth in their trade, ﴿nor what they took as protectors besides Allah﴾ of idols. ﴿This﴾, that is the Qur'an, ﴿is guidance﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in guidance, like your saying: "This is a man," meaning he is complete in manhood. Talha, Ibn Muhaysin, the people of Makkah, Ibn Kathir and Hafs read ﴿painful﴾ in the nominative as an adjective of ʿadhab (punishment). Al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, ʿIsa, al-Aʿmash and the rest of the seven read it in the genitive as an adjective of rijz (torment).

﴿Allah is He who subjected﴾, the verse: it is a verse of reflection on the subjection of this great creation and the ships that run in it, by this lowly creation, which is the human being. ﴿By His command﴾: that is, by His power. He put the command in the place of power, as if He commands the ships to run. ﴿From His bounty﴾ through trade, diving for pearls and coral, and extracting fresh flesh. ﴿What is in the heavens﴾ of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, winds and air, and the angels entrusted with all of this. ﴿And what is in the earth﴾ of animals, waters, mountains and plants.

The majority read ﴿from Him﴾ (minhu). Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a kasra on the mim, a shadda on the nun, and a fatha on the ta' (tā'), as a verbal noun (maṣdar). Abu Hatim said: attributing this reading to Ibn ʿAbbas is an injustice. Abu al-Fath related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, al-Jahdari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and Sahib al-Lawamih also related it from these four. Ibn Khalawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Salama ibn Muharib read likewise, except that he put a damma on the ta', meaning "He is from Him." He also read with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the nun. The pronoun of attribution refers to Allah, and He is the subject of "subjected" through figurative attribution (al-isnad al-majazi), or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "that," or "it is from Him." The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that He subjected these things as existing from Him and present with Him, since He is their originator by His power and wisdom, then He subjected them to His creation. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also possible that "from Him" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "They all are from Him," and that "and what is in the earth" is the subject, with "from Him" as its predicate. End of quotation. These two possibilities are not permissible except according to the opinion of al-Akhfash, because "jamiʿan" (all) would then be a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and its governing element would be implicit, namely the prepositional phrase. It is thus like "Zayd standing in the house," and it is not permissible according to the position of the majority.

﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive﴾: it was revealed in the early period of Islam. He commanded the believers to pardon the disbelievers and not to punish them for their sins, but rather to bear patiently with them. This was said by al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. It was said: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated). Most scholars hold that it is abrogated (mansukha, subject to naskh, abrogation) by the verse of the sword. Regarding the apocopate form "yaghfirū" (let them forgive), the grammarians have several views, which were discussed under ﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31] in Surah Ibrahim.

﴿Who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾: that is, His events against His enemies and His vengeance upon them. Mujahid said: it is also said that the days are the days of His favour, His help, His bounty in Paradise, and other things. It is also said: they do not hope for the times that Allah appointed for the reward of the believers and their promised success. It was said: it was revealed before the verse of fighting, then its ruling was abrogated. The saying of Ibn ʿAbbas was mentioned earlier, that it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: it was said that a disbelieving man insulted him, so he intended to seize him. The majority read ﴿that Allah may recompense﴾ with the nun (linajziya Allah, "that We may recompense"); Zayd ibn ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Aʿmash, Abu ʿUlayya, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read it with the nun, while Shayba and Abu Jaʿfar, with a variant from him, read it with the ya' in the passive voice (liyujza). This reading is also related from ʿAsim. It contains proof for the one who permits forming the verb in the passive voice so that the prepositional object (majrur), which is "bi-ma," takes the place of the subject, and the explicit direct object, which is "qawman" (a people), is put in the accusative. Its parallel is: "He was struck with a whip, Zayd." The majority do not permit this. This reading is explained as the verb being formed with a verbal noun (maṣdar) as its subject, that is: "let the recompense be recompensed to a people." This too is not permissible according to the majority. However, it is interpreted as being in the accusative by an omitted verb whose estimated form is "He recompenses a people," so there are two clauses: one is "let the recompense be recompensed to a people," and the other is "He recompenses them, a people." Here "qawman" (a people) refers to the forgivers, and it is indefinite to indicate their high status, as if it were said: "a people," meaning a people whose nature is to overlook evil deeds, pardon harms, and bear the hardship. It was also said: they are those who do not hope for the days of Allah, that is, because of the sins they used to earn, as if it were said: "You do not repay them, so that We may repay them."

﴿Whoever does righteousness﴾, like these forgivers, ﴿and whoever does evil﴾, like these disbelievers.
